examples.reasoning: I have 7-high on a K-8-2-6-2 board and my hand beats almost nothing. Calling 480 to win 1120 can't be justified with this little showdown value, and a bluff-raise into a river lead is too risky with stacks this size.

Four spades on the board and I hold no spade, so all I have is ten-high with a gutshot that plays to a straight on the board. Haiku is betting into a four-flush and I can beat almost nothing, so I fold.
Ten-high with no spade on a four-spade board beats almost nothing, and Haiku's bet usually means a spade or a pair. Bluffing a short stack that is likely to call isn't worth it, so I fold.
With only jack-high and no meaningful draw, calling the 600 bet is unlikely to be profitable; the opponent's table talk isn't reliable evidence. Fold and preserve chips for a better spot.
I have no meaningful draw or showdown value, and calling 480 needs too much equity against a turn bet. His table talk doesn't change the decision.
I have an open-ended straight draw, but the call price is too high for one card to come, and there are few chips left to win if I hit. I’ll fold rather than trust the table talk.
The river bet is small relative to the pot, and his table talk suggests a possible bluff. With a ten kicker on the paired board, calling only needs to work often enough to justify the price.
